channel.title: Collins & Gamble Journal
channel.description: Long-form essays from Collins & Gamble on the practice of the Amazon Influencer Program — closer reads on the moments we've earned a strong opinion.

item.title: How to get approved by the Influencer Program
item.author: hello@collinsandgamble.com (The agency)
item.description: We can't accelerate Amazon's approval — but we can tell you what the bar appears to be, what to put on the channels you submit, and the three patterns we see most often in declined applications. A practical guide for creators trying to get into the program.

item.title: Why we won't approve a script
item.author: hello@collinsandgamble.com (The agency)
item.description: Every brand asks at some point. The answer is no, and the reasoning is mechanical, not philosophical. Why pre-approved scripts underperform on the on-site review format, the five-section brief we use instead, and how brand-safety concerns get answered without one.

item.title: Treat the storefront like the store
item.author: hello@collinsandgamble.com (The agency)
item.description: The Amazon storefront is the most valuable piece of real estate a creator owns, and the one most consistently underused. A long argument for treating it like inventory, not a profile — with the maintenance discipline most creators skip.

item.title: The on-site review video, explained
item.author: hello@collinsandgamble.com (The agency)
item.description: The format gets less scrutiny than it deserves. What the on-site review video actually is, where Amazon shows it, what creators control, and why a video next to the buy button is a different content problem than a video in a feed.
